New plan: I incorrectly interpreted the question as asking for a comparison between the conditional probability $P(F \mid E)$ and the marginal probability $P(F)$. The question specifically asks if the chance is larger "when observing speaking english," which implies a comparison between the conditional probability given English, $P(F \mid E)$, and the conditional probability given *not* speaking English, $P(F \mid 
eg E)$. My previous calculation showed $P(F \mid E) \approx 0.511$, but I failed to calculate $P(F \mid 
eg E) = P(
eg E \cap F) / P(
eg E) = 0.08 / 0.10 = 0.80$. Since $0.511 < 0.80$, the chance is indeed lower when observing English. Next time, I will strictly compare the two conditional probabilities ($P(F \mid E)$ vs $P(F \mid 
eg E)$) to answer "Is the chance... larger when observing X?" rather than comparing against the marginal average. I will also ensure my final "Yes" or "No" aligns with this correct comparison.
